deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 78v is not a Riemann manuscript. It is a printed page, p. 300, from Thomas Babington Macaulay's 'History of England', Chapter III, 'State of England in 1685', in an American edition. It apparently became bound or filed into the 'R.Varia' bundle as wrapping or scrap paper. The neighbouring folio 78r (the previous page) is the preceding printed page 299.

The page continues Macaulay's account of the Restoration navy:
- He describes the 'tarpaulin' commanders as rough in manner and in speech.
- He says these men supplied the models for Smollett's Lieutenant Bowling and Commodore Trunnion.
- He claims that no Stuart naval officer combined seamanship with polish: 'the seamen were not gentlemen; and the gentlemen were not seamen.'
- He gives naval costs. The English navy could have been kept efficient for £380,000 a year, but £400,000 a year was actually spent. French naval costs were about the same and Dutch costs considerably more.
- He begins the section on the ordnance, noting it was then much cheaper relative to other military charges.
- A footnote cites Pepys's 1684 report (in manuscript at Magdalene College, Cambridge), Pepys's 'Memoirs relating to the State of the Royal Navy' (1688), and further sources: Sheffield, Teonge, Aubrey's Life of Monk, the Life of Sir Cloudesley Shovel (1708), and the Commons' Journals for 1683/4.

The only arithmetic content is implicit: the overspend is 400,000 − 380,000 = £20,000 a year. Nothing on the page was computed or written by Riemann; there are no handwritten annotations beyond stray marks.

The next page in the bundle is an 1894 letter from Leipzig, probably by Adolph Mayer given the Math. Annalen XVII reference. It concerns a Riemann letter to Gauss criticising Gauss's presentation of Pfaff's method. That letter is unrelated to this printed sheet.

results.what: Printed historical prose: Macaulay's History of England, vol. I, ch. III, p. 300, on the English navy and ordnance in 1685. Not mathematical and not by Riemann.

deep.surprise_reason: The folio is a printed page of Macaulay's History of England with no mathematical content and no Riemann handwriting. Its presence in the bundle is at most an archival curiosity (scrap or wrapper paper).

checkable.asserts: Actual naval expenditure (£400,000) exceeded the estimated efficient cost (£380,000) by £20,000 per year.
The efficient cost was 95% of the actual expenditure.

transcription_corrections: The final date in the footnote is the printed old-style/new-style double year '168 3/4', i.e. 1683/4 (March 1684 new style). It is not a mathematical fraction; '168$\frac{3}{4}$' should be read as 1683/4.
'Smollet' is as printed (a period spelling of Smollett), so it is not a transcription error.
Otherwise the transcription matches the image. The page is printed text, and stray marks in the left margin are not text.
